verdict.rationale: GitBook's own docs show a GitHub & GitLab Sync feature and describe Git workflows as built in, so docs can live in a user's Git repository. The evidence never shows that branches, pull requests or merges actually drive what gets published. Preview deployments are listed only as a bare feature name. Missing for 10: documented branch-to-space mapping, PR/merge-triggered publishing workflow, PR preview details tied to Git, independent hands-on corroboration of Git Sync.

support.subject: As a developer, my docs live in my own git repository — branches, pull requests, and merges drive what gets published

citations.quote: Write in the editor, drive it from your agent, or sync from Git.
